text:
raj_acme: Hey team — our Private deployment in prod-vpc can't pull models or reach telemetry since yesterday. API calls to the model registry timeout or fail with TLS errors, and our init scripts can't pip install packages. Example error from our worker:
```
requests.exceptions.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed (_ssl.c:XXXX)
during GET https://model-registry.redwood.ai/v1/models/abc123
``` 
We already opened outbound 443 in the firewall but the corp TLS proxy does SNI rewrite/inspection. Any quick allowlist or SNI guidance? We're blocked for a client release.

maria_support: Sorry you're blocked — we'll help triage. First things we'll need:
- curl -v to the registry from one of your nodes
- output of `openssl s_client -connect model-registry.redwood.ai:443 -servername model-registry.redwood.ai`
Also, temporary workaround: if you can allow SNI passthrough (no interception) for our key hosts that's ideal. If not possible, we can provide FQDNs and recommended ports to allow.

raj_acme: Here's the curl from a node (sanitized):
```
curl -v https://model-registry.redwood.ai/v1/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://model-registry.redwood.ai/v1/health
*   Trying 10.10.10.10...
* Connected to model-registry.redwood.ai (10.10.10.10) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake failed: certificate subject: CN=corp-proxy.local
* Closing connection 0
curl: (56) SSL: certificate subject CN=corp-proxy.local
```
So the TLS proxy is presenting its own cert (CN=corp-proxy.local) and client fails CN check.

devin_ops: That explains it — our services rely on SNI for routing and certificate pinning in some clients. Allowlist these FQDNs (outbound TCP 443) and ensure the TLS proxy does passthrough or presents the original cert for these domains (no re-signing):
```
- model-registry.redwood.ai
- registry-cdn.redwood.ai
- telemetry.ingest.redwood.ai
- auth.redwood.ai
- packages.redwood.ai
- files.pythonhosted.org
- pypi.org
- storage.googleapis.com (for model shards)
- registry-1.docker.io
- auth.docker.io
```
Prefer FQDN-based allowlist / SNI allowlist. If only IPs are possible, tell us and we'll provide current IP ranges (note: we use Cloudflare + GCS + AWS CDN for some endpoints — IPs change). Ports: TCP/443 (HTTPS). For apt you may need TCP/80 for redirects (deb endpoints).

maria_support: Commands to validate from your side:
```
# check SNI cert chain
openssl s_client -connect model-registry.redwood.ai:443 -servername model-registry.redwood.ai

# basic HTTP check
curl -v -H "Host: model-registry.redwood.ai" https://<proxy-ip>/v1/health
```
If openssl shows the proxy cert (CN != model-registry.redwood.ai) then the interceptor is terminating TLS. You need passthrough for the host or a TLS cert that contains the real SANs.

tess_security: Quick security note: we do NOT recommend disabling TLS verification in production. If you need a temporary stopgap to finish the deploy, you can disable telemetry (non-production) to reduce calls to our ingest endpoint: set `REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false` in the agent env and restart the agent. But only as a short-term measure. Long-term solution = SNI passthrough or trusted CA on the proxy that signs certificates with the proper SANs (and you add that CA to the host truststore).

raj_acme: Thanks. Our infosec won't do passthrough globally but agrees to add an SNI allowlist for specific hosts. We added the domains above and allowed TCP/443. After that, `openssl s_client` now returns a cert with CN=model-registry.redwood.ai and `curl` to /v1/health returns 200.

deploy-bot: Ticket #SUP-2026 created for tracking + automated checks scheduled.

raj_acme: Confirmed — model pulls and pip installs work. Deploy succeeded and telemetry is flowing. Thank you all! :tada:
